chapter: WDSU radio and the New Orleans scene
title: A Mississippi dinner and the 'we Christians' remark
summary: Returning from New York, dining with a Mississippi family, he is shaken when the hostess, quizzing him about Italy, says 'we Christians don't do things that way'.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: You've heard them. Well, let's see, I made some questions up. I might as well ask about those. What about that lady you met in Mississippi, Southern Bell?

Oh. Oh, yes. You mean the time I came? Well, I took a trip to New York, and on the way down back to New Orleans, I stopped at some friends in Mississippi. Yeah, yeah. Well, that shook me up pretty bad. If I remember correctly, I was invited.

for supper at a real southern Mississippi family's house and of course his friend had been invited along too, you know, and well they were very hospitable, you know, and all that and we were having dinner and everything was going along fine until, oh, I think we were carrying a conversation about Italy and this lady of course kept shooting questions at me about Italy, she wanted to know what the people did and how they did it and all that and then came the bomb and she says, well, we Christians don't do things that way. That really shook me up man. I really didn't know what to say.
